description.value: Patients with dementia who have dissociations in verbal and non-verbal sound processing were studied to investigate the anatomical basis of non-verbal perception using auditory cognitive tests and voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: Because environmental sound and music perception is so variable, this study aimed to explore the relationships of non-verbal sound perception in different dementia sub-groups and provide anatomical correlations using auditory cognitive tests and voxel-based morphometry (VBM).

description.value: This study included patients with Alzheimer’s dementia, behavior variant fronto-temporal dementia, and semantic dementia, together with age-matched controls, in a cross-sectional observational design.

spans.text: To determine the neuronal networks on non-verbal perception, 16 patients with Alzheimer’s dementia (AD), 15 with behavior variant fronto-temporal dementia (bv-FTD), 14 with semantic dementia (SD) were evaluated and compared with 15 age-matched controls.

description.value: Same-different discrimination test using scale-violated melodies from the Montreal Battery of Evaluation of Amusia; participants completed 31 paired melodies.
Clinical diagnosis was determined using detailed history, neurologic examination, a 1-hour neuropsychological battery, laboratory screening, and visual inspection of 3.0-tesla brain MRI.
Participants completed pitch discrimination, melody perception, and environmental sound naming and picture-matching tests using a desktop computer and two speakers.

instructions.value: Participants followed oral instructions and responded on answer sheets; melody and pitch trials required same-different judgments, while environmental sounds required verbal naming and picture selection.

stimuli.value: Paired tones, scale-violated melodies, and 55 environmental sounds with corresponding pictures.
